rows.question: Can I resit an exam I already passed to get a higher grade?
rows.answer: According to the rules for the AI for Security course [1], there is no provision for resitting an exam that you have already passed to get a higher grade. The resit is only available if you do not meet the minimum grade requirements for the exam (5.5) [1].

rows.question: Is a final mark of 5.45 a pass?
rows.answer: A final mark of 5.45 would not be considered a pass, as it is below the rounding threshold of 5.50, and would therefore be rounded down to 5.00 [1].

rows.question: When am I allowed to start my Master Project AI?
rows.answer: You are allowed to start your Master Project AI after having completed 60 ECTS of the MSc Artificial Intelligence program [3]. Additionally, the project typically begins after the Master's programme has started on 1 September [2].

rows.question: How many EC is the Master Project AI?
rows.answer: The Master Project AI is worth 30 EC (30 ECTS credits) [1].

rows.question: Can I redo the Evolutionary Computing programming assignment if I fail it?
rows.answer: No, you cannot redo the Evolutionary Computing programming assignment if you fail it. According to the course rules [1], there is no resit possible for the programming assignment.

rows.question: If I pass the Evolutionary Computing exam but fail the assignment, do I lose my exam grade?
rows.answer: No, if you pass the exam but fail the programming assignment, you can keep the grade of the passed exam component for next year or later. Then, you can pass the course by getting a good grade (> 5.5) for the missing assignment and using the old exam grade in the averaging formula [1].

rows.question: How is Deep Learning graded?
rows.answer: Deep Learning (XM_0083) is graded based on a final exam (50%) and practical assignments (50%). The final exam must be passed with a sufficient grade (equivalent to a grade of 5.5 or higher), and there is a resit available for the exam. [1]

rows.question: Who coordinates the Evolutionary Computing course?
rows.answer: The Evolutionary Computing course is coordinated by prof. dr. A.E. Eiben [3].

rows.question: I already completed Advanced Machine Learning. Can I take Mathematical Foundations of Machine Learning?
rows.answer: You can still take Mathematical Foundations of Machine Learning even if you have completed Advanced Machine Learning, as there are no specific prerequisites mentioned in the course rules [1]. However, note that the course covers a broad range of machine learning techniques, including both supervised and unsupervised learning, and you will need to be prepared to engage with these topics [1][3].

rows.question: What is the deadline to request an extra exam opportunity, and who qualifies?
rows.answer: According to [1], you must submit a request for an additional examination opportunity no later than 15 July. This applies if you have completed all but one unit of education to meet the requirements of the degree and have failed the examination during all previously offered attempts, unless participation in an examination was not possible for compelling reasons.

rows.question: How long after an exam can I inspect my graded work?
rows.answer: You have the right to inspect your graded examination within twenty working days after the results are announced, but no later than ten working days before the resit opportunity [1].

rows.question: How long does an examiner have to grade a written exam?
rows.answer: According to the general programme rules [1], an examiner has up to fifteen working days to determine the result of a written examination.

rows.question: I have a CS bachelor. Should I take Cognitive Psychology and its Applications or Skills for AI?
rows.answer: Based on the programme rules, as a student with an Artificial Intelligence/Computer Science bachelor degree, you should choose the course Cognitive Psychology and its Applications [1]. This course is a core component of the MSc Artificial Intelligence programme and contributes to key qualifications for graduates [2][3].

rows.question: Is there a resit for the group homework in Multi-Agent Systems?
rows.answer: No, there is no resit for the group homework assignments in Multi-Agent Systems [1].

rows.question: If I fail AI and Society, can I do a resit?
rows.answer: According to the course rules for AI and Society [2][4], if you fail the course, you can do a resit. However, the final product of the course, such as the opinion article, must be written in a controlled setting, and the use of generative AI is permitted in a limited way, with explicit disclosure required.

rows.question: How much does the final essay count for in AI and Society?
rows.answer: The final essay, which is the course's final product, counts for 50% of the final grade in AI and Society [2][4].

rows.question: Can I retake an NLP practical assignment to improve my grade?
rows.answer: No, you cannot retake an NLP practical assignment to improve your grade. According to the Natural Language Processing course rules [1], retakes of practical assignments to improve the grade are not allowed.

rows.question: What happens if I hand in an NLP assignment a few hours late?
rows.answer: If you hand in an NLP assignment a few hours late, it will be assessed a 10% penalty [1]. However, assignments will still be accepted up to 24 hours after the deadline [1].

rows.question: In which period is Natural Language Processing taught?
rows.answer: Natural Language Processing (XM_0121) is taught in period P5, as stated in source [3].

rows.question: What grade do I need on each part of Knowledge Representation?
rows.answer: You need a minimum grade of 5.5 for each component of the Knowledge Representation course, including weekly homework (15%), assignments in groups (35%), and the written exam (50%). A peer reviewing assignment report is also required, but it is marked pass/fail [2].

rows.question: I failed Experimental Design and Data Analysis. What can I retake?
rows.answer: If you failed Experimental Design and Data Analysis, you can only retake the individual digital test [1][2].

rows.question: What level is the Machine Learning for Graphs course?

rows.question: What do I need to pass Econometrics for Quantitative Finance?
rows.answer: To pass Econometrics for Quantitative Finance, you need to master the required mathematical and statistical knowledge, be able to apply basic econometric models, and understand their results [1][2]. Additionally, you should be prepared to implement these methods in case assignments using Python or another matrix-oriented programming language of your choice [1][3].

rows.question: Can I get an exemption from my master's thesis?
rows.answer: According to the rules, you cannot get an exemption from your master's thesis. The Examination Board does not have the authority to exempt students from the final project, which includes the thesis [1].

rows.question: How long do my passed exam results stay valid?
rows.answer: Your passed exam results are generally valid indefinitely, unless otherwise specified [1]. However, if your knowledge or skills are deemed outdated, the Examination Board may require a supplementary or replacement examination [2].

rows.question: Will there be a second examiner at my oral exam?
rows.answer: Yes, there will be a second examiner at your oral exam, unless the Examination Board has determined otherwise [1].

rows.question: How quickly will I get the result of an oral exam?
rows.answer: You will receive the result of an oral exam as soon as possible, but at the latest within two working days after the examination has finished [1][2].

rows.question: I have dyslexia. What do I need to submit to get exam facilities?
rows.answer: You need to provide a statement from a BIG-, NIP-, or NVO-registered professional who is qualified to conduct a psychological evaluation, as stated in [1][3].

rows.question: What IELTS score do I need to be admitted?
rows.answer: You need an IELTS Academic overall score of at least 6.5, with a minimum score of 6.0 for each subcomponent (Listening, Reading, Writing, and Speaking) to meet the English language requirement for admission [1].

rows.question: How many EC is the whole AI master's programme?
rows.answer: The entire AI master's programme is worth 120 EC (120 ECTS credits), as stated in the teaching and examination regulation [4].

rows.question: Which specialisations can I choose in the AI master?
rows.answer: You can choose between the main track AI, Cognitive Science, or AI for Health specialisations [1].

rows.question: Who decides if my situation isn't covered by the exam regulations?
rows.answer: In instances not regulated by the Teaching and Examination Regulations or in the event of demonstrable extreme unreasonableness or unfairness, the faculty board responsible for the study programme will decide, unless the matter concerned is the responsibility of the Examination Board [1].

rows.question: How soon after the first exam's results can the resit be held?
rows.answer: According to the rules stated in [1], the resit for a (partial) examination may not take place within ten working days of the announcement of the results for the original (partial) examination. This rule applies to the final exam as well [1][4].

rows.question: Can I take an elective that isn't on the programme's list?
rows.answer: No, you cannot take an elective that isn't on the programme's list. According to the transitional provisions [1], certain courses have been discontinued and removed from the curriculum, and the programme rules do not allow for electives outside of the specified list.

rows.question: The regulations say there are two exam opportunities per year. Does that mean I can resit the AI and Society essay?
rows.answer: Yes, you are allowed to resit the AI and Society essay as there are two examination opportunities per academic year according to the regulations [1].1a. However, note that this applies to the unit of education as a whole, so you would need to have failed the original attempt to qualify for a resit.

rows.answer: Based on the information provided in [1], you are not directly admissible to the Master's programme in Artificial Intelligence with only 12 ECTS in AI key area courses, as it requires at least 18 ECTS [1][1].

rows.question: I'm in the Cognitive Science specialisation and have 48 EC. Can I start my master thesis?
rows.answer: No, you cannot start your master thesis with only 48 ECTS. According to the rules, you need to have completed a total of 60 ECTS from the MSc Artificial Intelligence before you are admitted to the master thesis [1][2].
